obligations.expected_behavior: Bind every replay result to a complete Current Snapshot.
forbidden_result: A replay result is produced without a complete Current Snapshot binding.
The binding covers only a partial Current Snapshot.
obligations.observable_result: The replay result records or exposes an association with a complete Current Snapshot.
obligations.state_after: The replay result is bound to a complete Current Snapshot.
obligations.state_before: A replay result is being produced or consumed and its Current Snapshot binding has not yet been established.
obligations.subject: Replay result
obligations.trigger: When a replay result is produced or consumed.

obligations.expected_behavior: Reproduce the replay result from a fresh checkout.
forbidden_result: Replay succeeds only from a previously modified or stateful checkout.
A fresh checkout cannot reproduce the replay result.
obligations.observable_result: Running the replay from a fresh checkout yields the recorded result.
obligations.state_after: The replay result is reproduced from a fresh checkout.
obligations.state_before: A replay result exists and a fresh checkout is available for replay.
obligations.subject: Replay execution
obligations.trigger: When replay is run from a fresh checkout.

obligations.expected_behavior: If result-determining input drift is detected and remains unexplained, mark the result stale or fail closed.
forbidden_result: An unexplained result-determining input drift is ignored.
The result is treated as current and valid despite unexplained result-determining input drift.
Replay continues as successful without a stale designation or fail-closed outcome.
obligations.observable_result: The affected result is marked stale or the replay path refuses to proceed and fails closed.
obligations.state_after: The result is stale or the replay path has failed closed.
obligations.state_before: A replay result exists and result-determining input drift is present without an explanation.
obligations.subject: Replay result validity
obligations.trigger: When unexplained drift occurs in an input that determines the result.
